== Biography ==

The Queen of Ev, also known simply as the Queen, is the mother of ten children and the former ruler of the land of Ev prior to her captivity. Ozma of Oz describes her as "the poor Queen of Ev and her ten children," whose rescue prompts an expedition into the underground realm of the Nome King.

According to the Nome King himself, the Queen and her children were enslaved and, because they were "delicate and tender," transformed into articles of ornament and bric-a-brac scattered throughout his palace, where they served only as decoration rather than as laborers. The Nome King further explains that instead of enchanting the family all at once, he allowed her rescuers to guess among his ornaments one at a time, since, in his words, "it serves to keep me amused for a long time."

Once freed, the Queen returns with her ten children to the royal palace of Ev, where a crowd of subjects gathers to welcome her with cheering and flowers. She graciously allows Princess Langwidere to keep her mirrored chamber and her cabinet of heads, relieving Langwidere of her former duties to the people of Ev. The Queen then presents her eldest son to the assembled subjects from a balcony, declaring him "your future ruler, King Evardo Fifteenth," a boy of fifteen years who becomes the fifteenth Evardo to rule Ev.

== Narrative role ==

Before her rescue, the Queen of Ev and her ten children had been enslaved by the Nome King, who transformed them all into articles of ornament and bric-a-brac scattered through the rooms of his palace. Ozma of Oz leads an expedition — Dorothy, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, Tiktok, Billina, the Cowardly Lion, and an army of Oz — to free the Queen of Ev and her ten children from the Nome King's underground palace. There, visitors are required to guess which ornaments conceal the enchanted royal family, one guess at a time. Dorothy is allowed to guess and succeeds in freeing Prince Evring, the youngest son of the Queen of Ev, a step toward disenchanting the rest of the family. Once restored, the Queen returns with her ten children to the royal palace of Ev, where a crowd gathers to welcome them with cheering and flowers. There she encounters Princess Langwidere, who has governed in her absence and is relieved to set aside her duties; the Queen graciously permits Langwidere to keep her rooms and her cabinet of heads. Taking her eldest son out onto a balcony before the assembled subjects, the Queen presents him as their future ruler, and he is crowned King Evardo Fifteenth of Ev, fifteen years old and bearing fifteen silver buckles on his jacket as the fifteenth Evardo to rule the land.

== Personality ==

The Queen of Ev shows graciousness toward those who might have given her cause for resentment: once freed, she permits Princess Langwidere, who had governed in her place, to keep her private rooms and her cabinet of heads for as long as she lives, extending courtesy rather than reclaiming her former position by force.

She also displays a formal, ceremonial pride in her family. Presenting her eldest son to the assembled crowd from a balcony, she declares him "your future ruler, King Evardo Fifteenth," specifying his age and the number of silver buckles on his jacket — a precise, public framing of the moment rather than a private family scene.

According to the Nome King, who held her captive, she and her children were "delicate and tender," a description he used to justify transforming them into ornaments instead of setting them to hard labor. As this characterization comes from her captor's own self-serving account, it reflects his view of her rather than an established fact about her nature.

== Appearance ==

The excerpts give little direct physical description of the Queen. The Nome King, explaining why he chose to enchant her and her ten children into ornaments rather than set them to labor, describes them as delicate and tender — a characterization offered by her captor to justify his own treatment of her, not an independent account of her person.

== Relationships ==

'''[[Nome King]]''' — enemy. The Nome King transformed the Queen and her children into ornaments and bric-a-brac, scattering them through his palace under the claim of sparing "delicate and tender" slaves from hard labor — an account that casts him as her captor.

'''[[Evardo]]''' — family. Evardo is the Queen's eldest son; she presents him to the people of Ev from the palace balcony as "your future ruler, King Evardo Fifteenth."

'''[[King]]''' — family. The relationship seems to be that of husband and wife: the former King of Ev is described as having "a perfect right to sell his family" — the Queen and her ten children — to the Nome King in exchange for a long life.

'''[[Prince]]''' — family. The Prince, who gives his name as Evring, recalls that his father sold his mother and all her children to the Nome King, identifying the Queen as his mother among those enslaved.

'''[[BILLINA]]''' — ally. Billina appears to have had a hand in freeing the Queen from captivity, reportedly telling her, "I've saved you from the Nome King, and you are a slave no longer."

== Trivia ==

* The Nome King transformed the Queen and her children into ornaments and bric-a-brac specifically because he judged them "delicate and tender" and unsuited to hard labor as slaves.
* Upon her return to the royal palace of Ev, the Queen graciously permitted Princess Langwidere to keep her own rooms and her cabinet of heads for as long as she lived.
* When she presented her eldest son to the people as their future ruler, he became King Evardo Fifteenth — fifteen years of age, wearing fifteen silver buckles on his jacket, and the fifteenth Evardo to rule the land of Ev.
